newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska says Sandvik funds to go to shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Skanska says Sandvik funds to go to shareholders.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska said on Monday that it was selling its stake of about 20 percent in tool maker/engineer Sandvik to finance its planned transfer of capital to shareholders.

"We have already announced that we were going to transfer capital worth 8-10 billion crowns to shareholders. The share portfolio has to finance this," Bo Ingvarsson, head of finance at Skanska, told Reuters.
Skanska plans to liquidate the rest of its share portfolio.
"There is not so much left in the portfolio after the sale of the Sandvik shares," Ingvarsson said.
"What we will do with the remaining shares, we will say when we have acted," Ingvarsson said.
Skanska has shares in ball bearing manufacturer SKF of a total market value of about 1.7 billion crowns and various stakes in smaller construction and real estate companies.
Skanska said on Monday it was selling over half its 10 billion crown holding in Sandvik to Swedish investor Industrivarden and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
It will also guarantee a Sandvik share redemption worth four billion crowns pledging 23.5 million Sandvik shares and so fully subscribing the offer.
